---
title: "Collapsing a pipeline"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
run_targets <- requireNamespace("targets", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("withr", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = run_targets,
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 3.2,
  dpi = 120
)
# size each plot chunk from the plot itself (ggtargets::dag_size()), so
# nodes, lines and text look the same in every figure
knitr::opts_hooks$set(dag_fig = function(options) {
  code <- paste(options$code, collapse = "\n")
  if (!isTRUE(options$eval) || !grepl("ggplot_dag|tar_ggplot", code)) {
    return(options)
  }
  seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", globalenv())) {
    get(".Random.seed", globalenv())
  }
  wd <- getwd()
  on.exit({
    setwd(wd)
    if (is.null(seed)) {
      suppressWarnings(rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
    } else {
      assign(".Random.seed", seed, globalenv())
    }
  })
  root <- knitr::opts_knit$get("root.dir")
  if (!is.null(root)) {
    setwd(root)
  }
  size <- tryCatch(
    {
      p <- eval(parse(text = code), new.env(parent = knitr::knit_global()))
      if (ggplot2::is_ggplot(p) && !inherits(p, "patchwork")) {
        ggtargets::dag_size(p)
      }
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(size)) {
    options$fig.width <- size[["width"]]
    options$fig.height <- size[["height"]]
  }
  options
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dag_fig = TRUE)
if (run_targets) {
  proj_dir <- tempfile("ggtargets-collapsing-")
  dir.create(proj_dir)
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = proj_dir)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggtargets)
library(targets)
```

A pipeline with too many targets can be hard to read. But, if the targets can be categorized into a handful of stages (ingest, model, report etc.), a collapsed graph can be generated with one node per stage. `tar_ggplot(collapse_by = )` and `dag_collapse()` allow to collapse the targets that share a value of a column into a single node, and the dependencies between the groups become one edge each.

## Where the stages come from

`targets` has no tag or category field for a target. It has one free-form text field, `description`, and that is where a stage goes for now. `tar_network()` returns it as a column, and `tar_dag()` keeps it, so `collapse_by = "description"` works as it is.

A description is set for one target with the `description` argument of `tar_target()`. Targets with the same text are one stage:

```{r}
#| label: description-target
#| eval: false
list(
  tar_target(raw_a, load_raw(1), description = "ingest"),
  tar_target(clean_a, clean(raw_a), description = "ingest"),
  tar_target(fit_1, fit(clean_a), description = "model")
)
```

Writing it for every target gets repetitive in a larger pipeline. `tar_option_set(description = )` sets the description of every target defined after it, so a stage is written once, for a block of targets. A `description` given to `tar_target()` still takes precedence over the option for that target. The pipeline below has three stages, set a block at a time, and ends with a reset, `tar_option_set(description = character(0))`, so that nothing after the last block gets a stage by accident. `config` comes first, before any description is set, so it has none:

```{r}
#| label: pipeline
tar_script({
  load_raw <- function(seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    rnorm(20)
  }
  # its own loader, so that a later edit touches only raw_b
  load_b <- function() {
    set.seed(2)
    rnorm(20)
  }
  clean <- function(x) x[abs(x) < 3]
  combine2 <- function(a, b) c(a, b)
  fit <- function(x, shift = 0) mean(x) + shift
  render <- function(x, y) paste(round(mean(x), 3), round(mean(y), 3))

  config_targets <- list(tar_target(config, list(shift = 1)))

  tar_option_set(description = "ingest")
  ingest_targets <- list(
    tar_target(raw_a, load_raw(1)),
    tar_target(raw_b, load_b()),
    tar_target(clean_a, clean(raw_a)),
    tar_target(clean_b, clean(raw_b))
  )

  tar_option_set(description = "model")
  model_targets <- list(
    tar_target(features, combine2(clean_a, clean_b)),
    tar_target(fit_1, fit(features, config$shift)),
    tar_target(fit_2, fit(features))
  )

  tar_option_set(description = "report")
  report_targets <- list(
    tar_target(summary_all, combine2(fit_1, fit_2)),
    tar_target(report_doc, render(summary_all, features))
  )

  tar_option_set(description = character(0))
  c(config_targets, ingest_targets, model_targets, report_targets)
})
```

The pipeline as it is, one row per target:

```{r}
#| label: full
#| fig-alt: "The pipeline of ten targets, one per row: config, raw_a, raw_b, clean_a, clean_b, features, fit_1, fit_2, summary_all and report_doc, in different colors, joined by lines that bend and cross."
tar_ggplot()
```

## One node per stage

With `collapse_by = "description"` the targets of a stage are one node, named after the stage, with the number of targets in its label. `config`, which has no description, stays as it is:

```{r}
#| label: collapsed
#| fig-alt: "The collapsed graph: four nodes, one per row, ingest (4), config, model (3) and report (2), with lines from ingest and config to model and from model to report."
tar_ggplot(collapse_by = "description")
```

`n`, the number of targets in a node and of dependencies in an edge, can set the size of a node and the width of an edge with `node_size = "n"` and `edge_width = "n"`. `node_color = "description"` colors the nodes by stage:

```{r}
#| label: sized
#| fig-alt: "The same four nodes, now of different sizes, the largest for ingest and the smallest for config, joined by lines of different widths, the widest from model to report. Ingest, model and report each have a color, named in a legend, and config, which has no stage, is gray."
tar_ggplot(
  collapse_by = "description",
  node_color = "description",
  node_size = "n",
  edge_width = "n"
)
```

The same collapsed graph from a `dag`, for when you also want to look at or change the nodes first:

```{r}
#| label: dag-collapse
d <- tar_dag()
small <- dag_collapse(d, "description")
small$nodes[c("name", "label", "n")]
small$edges
```

## Colors and status

A node can be colored by build status, as for the full pipeline. A stage whose targets all have the same status shows it, and the collapsed graph after a build is all up to date:

```{r}
#| label: build
tar_make(reporter = "silent")
```

```{r}
#| label: status-uptodate
#| fig-alt: "The four nodes of the collapsed graph, all in the up to date color, with a legend."
tar_ggplot(
  collapse_by = "description",
  node_color = "status",
  palette = targets_status_colors()
)
```

Now `load_b()` changes (here with a text substitution in `_targets.R`, in place of editing the file). `raw_b` and everything that depends on it are outdated, but `raw_a` is not, so the targets of the ingest stage no longer share a status:

```{r}
#| label: edit
script <- readLines("_targets.R")
writeLines(sub("set.seed(2)", "set.seed(3)", script, fixed = TRUE), "_targets.R")
```

```{r}
#| label: status-mixed
#| fig-alt: "The collapsed graph after the edit: model and report in the outdated color, config in the up to date color, and ingest in gray, which is not in the legend."
tar_ggplot(
  collapse_by = "description",
  node_color = "status",
  palette = targets_status_colors()
)
```

A stage with different statuses has no status of its own, so it is drawn gray, without an entry in the legend. Its lines are still there. The same goes for any node that has no value in the column `node_color` names. (The gray is the one `targets_status_colors()` uses for the `none` status, of the functions and objects that `targets_only = FALSE` adds, so with both in one plot a gray node can be either.)

## Things to know

- **End a block of descriptions with a reset.** `tar_option_set(description = character(0))` puts the default back. Without it, the option stays set for every target defined after the block, including those in files loaded later with `tar_source()`.
- **`tarchetypes::tar_map()` changes the description.** By default (`descriptions = tidyselect::everything()`) it appends the mapped values to each description, `"ingest 1 x"`, so the targets it makes would each be a stage of their own. Pass `descriptions = NULL` to keep the stage's description.
- **The descriptions must match exactly.** `"ingest"` and `"Ingest "` are two stages.
- **A target with no description is a node of its own.** A stage can't have the name of such a target: that is an error, because the two would be merged.
- **`description` is also the label of a target** in `tar_manifest()` and `tar_visnetwork()`. A short stage name is a good description there. A sentence is a poor key.

## Metadata of your own

`targets` can't carry any other field for a target, but a column can be added to the nodes of `tar_dag()`'s result, and `dag_collapse()` takes any column. Here, two people own some of the targets, and the rest have no owner:

```{r}
#| label: own-column
#| fig-alt: "A summary by owner: the nodes ana (3) and ben (2), in red and yellow with a legend of the two owners, above the five targets that have no owner (features, fit_1, fit_2, summary_all and report_doc). Those are small and gray, and joined by lines in the owners' colors and in gray."
d <- tar_dag()
owner <- c(config = "ana", raw_a = "ana", clean_a = "ana", raw_b = "ben", clean_b = "ben")
d$nodes$owner <- unname(owner[d$nodes$name]) # NA for the rest
ggplot_dag(dag_collapse(d, "owner"), node_color = "owner", node_size = "n")
```

The targets without an owner stay as they are, in gray. The names `row`, `col`, `x`, `y` and `color_index` can't be used for a column: the layout keeps them for its own.

## When stages depend on each other both ways

If one stage has a target that depends on a target of another stage, and that stage has a target that depends back on the first, the collapsed graph would have a loop, which a DAG can't have. That is an error, and it names the stages and the edges behind it:

```{r}
#| label: cycle
tar_script(list(
  tar_target(a1, 1, description = "A"),
  tar_target(b1, a1, description = "B"),
  tar_target(a2, b1, description = "A")
))
try(tar_ggplot(collapse_by = "description"))
```

Either of the two targets of stage A can be moved into a stage of its own, or into stage B, to break the loop. `tar_ggplot()` without `collapse_by` still draws the pipeline.
